podcast.title: Radio Market Saturation
podcast.body: According to NPR contributor Felix Contreras, mainstream radio in the 1970s seemed to only have room for one Latin rock band, a slot already occupied by Santana, which may have limited the success of other talented groups like Molo. "Felix Contreras, our NPR contributor, believes that mainstream radio only had room for one Latin rock band, and that slot was already taken by his brother."

podcast.title: Richie Valens' Potential
podcast.body: Richie Valens's tragic death in 1959 deprived the music world of seeing where he might have taken Latin rock, as he was proud of his Mexican heritage and a significant early influence. "His death in that plane crash with Buddy Holly and the Big Bopper in 1959 was tragic on many levels. One of those being that had deprived us of where he might have taken Latin rock."
